outline.name: Halcyon LSAT study taxonomy (Logical Reasoning and Reading Comprehension question families)
outline.version: Halcyon's own list, LR01 to LR20 and RC01 to RC14, from courses/lsat/meta.js
outline.source: Reference read: LSAC skill descriptions at https://www.lsac.org/lsat/taking-lsat/test-format/logical-reasoning and https://www.lsac.org/lsat/taking-lsat/test-format/reading-comprehension; format page https://www.lsac.org/lsat/taking-lsat/test-format
outline.notes: LSAC does not publish this list. LR01 to RC14 are Halcyon's own study taxonomy, built from the question families teachers commonly use, and are not an LSAC outline. Halcyon is not affiliated with or endorsed by LSAC. The reference for what the sections test is LSAC's public description: for Logical Reasoning, ten skills such as identifying argument parts, spotting unstated assumptions, finding reasoning errors, judging how evidence affects an argument, applying principles, recognizing explanations and points of disagreement; for Reading Comprehension, ten skills such as main idea and purpose, stated details, inferences, meaning in context, organization, application, principles, analogies, author's attitude, and how new information affects claims, plus at most one comparative passage set per section. Every RC code maps to a stated LSAC RC skill. LSAC's format page (read 2026-11-07) says four 35 minute sections, three scored and one unscored, and that the test will change starting with the August 2027 administration; it does not state which scored sections are LR versus RC, so the 'two scored LR sections, one scored RC since August 2026' framing in meta.js was not confirmed from that page. IDs follow meta.js codes since no official numbering exists.
